mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when this trigger is met, or the trigger fires but returns are not statistically different from baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) contraction signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST monthly change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the trigger fires but returns are not statistically lower than baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months, combined with accelerating industrial production (INDPRO), signals a late-cycle economy where labor scarcity and capacity constraints push inflation higher and compress valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% for 3 consecutive months AND INDPRO > 0.3% monthly change
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than baseline during triggered periods, or the trigger fires but returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 1% for two consecutive months, in the absence of a corresponding decline in unemployment (UNRATE > 4%), signals supply-side disruptions that raise input costs and erode margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for 2 consecutive months AND UNRATE > 4%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the trigger does not precede statistically significant underperformance.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly decline in the federal funds rate below 2% signals an emergency easing in response to financial stress, which boosts liquidity and risk appetite, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not statistically higher than baseline during triggered emergency cuts, or the trigger fires but returns are negative in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 1% coincident with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a tightening labor market, which raises wage pressures and inflation expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as discount rates rise.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 1% AND UNRATE monthly change < -0.1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than baseline during triggered episodes, or the trigger does not precede negative returns in a majority of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above the 5-year average, combined with flat or declining personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1), indicates households are saving rather than spending, which reduces demand and pressures corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 5-year average for 3 consecutive months AND GDPC1 monthly change <= 0%
regime_hint: household deleveraging or precautionary savings regime
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than baseline during triggered periods, or the trigger fires but returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) above 4% for six consecutive months signals entrenched inflation, which prompts the Federal Reserve to maintain restrictive policy, depressing equity valuations through higher discount rates and raising input costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than baseline during periods of entrenched inflation, or the trigger does not precede negative returns in more than 50% of cases.
